Series Factory API Reference¶

Back to PlussQit API Reference

This page documents the pluss::series::* factory surface separately from the Series method reference.

That split is intentional.

  • The method reference answers: “I already have a Series; what can I do to it?”

  • The factory reference answers: “I do not have a Series yet; how do I build the right one?”

Those are different jobs, and mixing them on one landing page makes both harder to navigate.

What Lives Here¶

pluss::series::* is the construction namespace for numeric/boolean Series.

Use it for:

  • direct value construction with make

  • shape-first allocation like empty, zeros, ones, full

  • range/grid builders like arange, linspace, eye

  • random and distribution factories like rand, randn, randint, bernoulli, poisson, multinomial

  • like-factories such as zeros_like and randn_like

  • complex constructors such as complex and polar

Reading the Overloads¶

Many Series factories look wider than they really are because several public spellings funnel into the same underlying configuration path.

For the core families, the overload story usually collapses into one of three ideas:

  • explicit dtype: pluss::series::zeros({2, 3}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64)

  • explicit config: pluss::series::zeros({2, 3}, pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(...))

  • option-style sugar: typed tags or key/value config lists that ultimately build the same Config

So the handwritten pages document the canonical behavior first, then call out the overload quirks that materially change the result.

Current Coverage¶

The current handwritten factory batch now covers the public constructor families most users actually reach first and second:

  • direct value construction: make

  • shape-first constants and layouts: empty, zeros, ones, full, eye

  • range/grid builders: arange, linspace

  • like-factories: empty_like, zeros_like, ones_like, full_like, rand_like, randn_like, randint_like, eye_like

  • stochastic constructors: rand, randn, rand_btw, randint, normal, randperm, bernoulli, poisson, multinomial

  • complex constructors: complex, polar

Those pages are split this way on purpose.

  • The core random pages (rand, randn) teach seed and dtype policy.

  • The interval/discrete pages (rand_btw, randint, randperm) teach how those rules change once bounds or uniqueness matter.

  • The like-factory pages teach “same geometry as this existing tensor” as a separate mental model from ordinary shape-first construction.

  • The complex pages teach the pairwise “two real tensors in, one complex tensor out” surface, which behaves differently from the scalar-fill factories.

What is still out of scope for this handwritten batch is the unsupported sparse and quantized constructor stub family.
